Summary of the work before the final verdict.

**Change** (only `test/dogfood/queue.test.ts`, HEAD unchanged at `804e935`): `loopFixture()` now appends the `[user]` stanza to the fresh private repository's `.git/config` with `appendFile` instead of running two `git config` processes, and memoizes the per-file `which`/`where.exe git` lookup instead of repeating it per fixture. `.git/config` bytes and `GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT` were verified identical between the two approaches (`cmp` on two fresh `git init` repos); no user or global config is touched.

**Measurements** (same host, PATH `git` wrapper counting every process including the runtime adapters; evidence in `author-temp/measure/`): per-tuple setup Git processes 31 → 29 for all 16 modes, lifecycle counts identical mode-by-mode (e.g. `correction` 207, `spent-legacy-correction` 146). Interleaved control/candidate/control/candidate runs of the two formerly failing modes: setup ~205/197/201/210ms vs ~209/184/193/181ms; the ~10ms per-tuple saving is inside run noise locally. Full file: 6622 → 6472 Git processes, normalized op diff shows only `config user.name/email` 83 → 8 (the 8 remaining are updater clones, not fixture setup); 100/100 tests pass at 47.8s vs 48.3s base.

Gates: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm planning:check`, and `pnpm test` (887 passed, 3 skipped) all green.
